P	The village of Stonetop sits upon ancient ruins, built centuries or even millennia ago by the <b>Makers</b> world. Strange and alien things. Primordial things and primordial powers, from the very dawn of time.
H2	Themes
HR
P	Choose or roll 1, or 2 and combine.
P	1d12 theme
HR
P	1 Vastness, enormity, incomprehensibility, the primordial void
P	2 Truth, purity, quintessence, the raw stuff of creation
P	3 Fundamental forces: order, chaos, time, space, gravity, light, death, etc.
P	4 The spirit world: consciousness, symbols and thought, the connection of all things
P	5 True names, words of power, speech that transcends language
P	6 Celestial bodies: their movements, their mysteries, their influence on the world
P	7 Paradox: destiny and free will, causal loops, infinity, mutually exclusive truths
P	8 Natural forces and the shaping of the word: slow and subtle, violent and cataclysmic
P	9 The binding of the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412)
P	10 Mythic times and mythic deeds, the birth and death of gods and legends
P	11 Long-forgotten peoples/beings, from before the rise of the Makers
P	12 Portals, possibilities, other worlds, beings/things out of time and space (page 264). But there are things in the world that were old when the Makers were young. And there are things older still, older even than the world, bigger than the
H2	Hooks
B	A grand conjunction of the stars approaches, signaling momentous change.
B	A meteorite crashes not far from Stonetop.
B	A scholar returns from an ancient monument, preaching gibberish that infects the minds of others.
B	A ritual can be performed only at a site of primordial power.
B	Centuries ago, the spirit of War renounced their role and duties and incarnated as a reclusive shepherd, to live a simple life.
B	A sleeping titan—big as a mountain, covered in millennia of soil, debris, and growth—starts to stir.
B	A clan of refugees from no known region emerges from the portal below the <b>Ruined Tower</b> (page 332).
H2	Questions
HR
Q	The <b>Pale Hunter</b> (page 292) is associated with "the" moon, but are there other moons? What are they associated with?
Q	What tends to make you feel insignificant and small?
Q	Do you believe in fate? Or do we chart our own destinies?
Q	What strange place did you once visit that was clearly touched by ancient, eldritch powers?
PAGE	299
H2	Cosmology
HR
P	Many aspects of the setting's cosmology are intentionally left vague, for you and your group to flesh out as needed. Here are a few things to ask about or consider:
Q	How mythic is your cosmos? Like, is the sun a star, orbited by the world? Or does <b>Helior</b> (page 224) drive his chariot across the sky? Or what?
Q	Do other worlds float in the void? Can they be reached via the spirit world or <b>portals</b> (page 306)?
Q	What lies beyond the <b>Last Door</b> (page 70)? Is the afterlife the same for all, or do different fates await each soul?
Q	What exactly is the relationship between the First Creators, the great spirits, the gods of forgotten peoples, and the gods worshipped today?
Q	Did life evolve over eons? Or did the First Creators populate the world with much of the flora and fauna we know today? Or what?
Q	Where did humanity come from? Do we predate the Makers or were we made by them?
P	The answers to these questions will depend on how your players answer questions about other topics, and decisions you make about them. In particular, see <b>Aratis</b> (page 22), <b>Danu</b> (page 64), <b>Helior</b> (page 224), <b>Tor</b> (page 452), <b>gods and religion</b> (page 178), <b>death and the undying</b> (page 68), the <b>Makers</b> (page 264), <b>Lygos and the south</b> (page 256), and <b>Stonetop</b> itself (page 12).
H2	The First Creators
P	They were the first minds to know themselves, the first beings to give themselves names. They were born of the cosmic void, of light and possibility and the churning chaos of nothingness and all. They spoke reality into being, set down its fundamental laws. They made the world and bound the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412).
P	The First Creators are unlikely to feature directly in your game. Mostly, they serve as background, an excuse for why things are the way they are. Some might linger as what we now call <b>gods</b> (page 178), but as a rule they no longer actively shape the world.
P	Perhaps they have forgotten it entirely.
H2	The Things Below
HR
P	Beings of darkness, chaos, and corruption, older even than the First Creators. They are jealous and hateful and full of infinite malice, and so the First Creators bound them in the depths of the earth.
P	Though imprisoned, they still influence the world. The <b>Green Lords</b> (page 210) called on them when the <b>Fae</b> (page 94) rebelled. The servants of the <b>Stone Lords</b> (page 382) succumbed to their whispers and ushered in the <b>Time of Cataclysm</b> (page 413). The <b>Barrow Builders</b> (page 34) courted them openly and worshipped them as gods. Their influence has lessened in the <b>current age</b> (page 414), but it lingers still.
PAGE	300
H2	Great spirits
HR
P	Impossibly potent entities, numinous and grand. The First Creators made some as experiments, some to be companions, some to serve as stewards of the world. Other great spirits arose spontaneously, birthed from the cosmos or the beliefs of mortal beings.
P	Many of these great spirits are aloof, alien, and disinterested in the world (or at least, in this world). Others are active, but shape the world in subtle ways. Their numbers might well include the <b>Lady of Crows</b> (page 71), and some or all of the <b>major</b> <b>gods</b> (page 178).
P	To create a great spirit for your game, decide whether it's worshipped as a god.
P	If it is, create it using the procedure for <b>other gods</b> (page 184). Otherwise, pick or roll 2 primordial themes (page 298) and imagine the entity suggested by the combination. Consider why it goes unworshipped—is it unknown, uncaring, alien, or what?
P	Should one of the great spirits become active in your game, write it up as a threat (a <i>magical entity</i>). Even benevolent beings of such cosmic power can't help but cause trouble.
HR
H3	Incarnations
P	The great spirits sometimes manifest directly in the world. Such incarnations are likely to become figures of myth and legend. For examples, see:
B	The <b>Willow Witches</b> (page 120)
B	The <b>Nine-fingered stranger</b> (page 457) if you assume that Tor is a great spirit
B	The <b>Pale Hunter</b> (page 292), if you decide he's a primordial entity To create an incarnation, first establish what great spirit it's a manifestation of.
P	Then choose or roll for why it incarnated, its manifestation, and 1-3 constraints.
P	Write it up as a monster, and possibly as a threat, with all manner of powerful moves—such beings are not bound by the normal laws of reality. See the examples (previous column) for inspiration.
P	Be cautious about introducing incarnations into your game. They should make the world feel rich and mysterious and help you punctuate the PCs' lives with adventure; they should not overshadow the PCs, or serve as a convenient contrivance. Their involvement should always feel dangerous, fraught, and complicated.
P	1d12 why it incarnated
HR
P	1-2 As a punishment/penance/escape
P	3-4 Because potent magic summoned it
P	5-6 In pursuit of some agenda
P	7-8 Out of curiosity/boredom/despair
P	9-10 Through fate or cosmic accident
P	11-12 To learn, to experience the world
P	1d12 manifestation
HR
P	1-2 A seemingly normal person
P	3-4 A seemingly natural beast
P	5-6 A spirit or other mysterious being
P	7-8 A clearly supernatural person
P	9-10 A monster or supernatural beast, possibly a <b>titan</b> (page 303)
P	11-12 Roll 1d10 again, but it manifests as a group or multitude of the result

P	1d12 constraint
HR
P	1 Doesn't realize what it is
P	2 Is subservient to another
P	3-4 Has a <b>tether</b> (page 358)
P	5-7 Is bound by certain inviolate rules
P	8 Can incarnate only briefly, in or at certain circumstances/times
P	9 Is subject to mortal urges/needs/ emotions/weakness
P	10 Refuses to get involved
P	11 Is hunted by other supernatural beings
P	12 Can't use its power without dire consequences, for itself/the world

H2	Archons
HR
P	Archons are constructed <b>spirits</b> (page 358), made by the First Creators or one of the great spirits as guardians and enforcers of the cosmic order.
P	Start with the base archon stat block below. Pick or roll for their purpose, their manifestation, and up to 3 powers. Adjust the stat block to reflect these choices or results, writing at least one move to reflect its purpose and one to reflect it manifesting (unless its manifestation is a construct/ animate statue).

H2	Titans
HR
P	Legends speak of a time when beasts and beings of impossible scale roamed the world. The god <b>Tor</b> (page 452) is said to have slain three such beasts, and everyone knows about the skeleton on the side of <b>Titan Bones</b> (page 448).
P	Perhaps the First Creators placed these titans in the world. Perhaps they evolved amid the early world's riot of vitality and life. Some could have been incarnations of the great spirits, or <b>emanations</b> (page 436) of the Things Below.
P	Regardless, titans no longer roam the world like they once did. The <b>Crombil</b> (page 62) might be one, but it wakes only once every few decades. The <b>Suileach</b> (page 93) might be another, but it is confined to the Dread River. The hidden lands around the <b>Golden Oak</b> (page 186) are full of gargantuan beasts, but whether they are truly titans is up to you.
P	There might be other such titans, hidden away in remote corners of the world, sleeping the centuries away, waiting to rise once more.

H2	Sites
HR
P	There are places in the world marked or marred by primordial power. If such a site needs to be established, combine the terrain in which it's located with a marker.
P	1d12 marker
HR

P	8-9 Ruin(s) of the <b>Makers</b> (page 264), built near or around it
P	10 Mysterious structure(s), placed by primordial entities
P	11-12 Roll 1d10 twice and combine Once the site itself is established, pick or roll for a theme (page 298), an origin, and 1-3 features that make it interesting.
P	1d12 origin
HR
P	1-2 The intent of a (the) great spirit(s)
P	3-4 A confluence of geomantic/cosmic/ celestial forces
P	5-6 A conflict between mythic beings

P	11-12 The working (successful or not) of a potent spell or artifice
P	1d12 features
HR
P	1 An <b>archon</b> (page 302), watching over it or what it contains

P	3 An abundance of certain spirits
P	4 The <b>shade</b> (page 85) of a dead god or primordial entity, easily called up
P	5 Anomalies (time loops or fluxes, spatial warps, weird gravity, thoughts projected out loud, etc.)
P	6 A thin barrier with the spirit world
P	7 A <b>portal</b> (page 306), or a place with the potential for one
P	8 A font of power; a good place to work particular types of magic
P	9 Visions/omens/prophecies/insights, sometimes bestowed on visitors
P	10 <b>Useful or valuable flora</b> (page 458), something weird, found only here
P	11 The raw stuff of creation: <b>black</b> <b>iron</b> (page 307), water of life, <b>primordial flame</b> (page 311), etc.
P	12 One or more <b>artifacts</b> of primordial power (page 308) If such a site lies near areas that are or were once populated, consider the locals' attitudes towards it (reverence, awe, terror, avoidance, etc.), and what additional signs they might have left.

H3	Other sites of primordial power
B	A small lake: cold, acidic, devoid of life. During thick mists, it connects to other times, places, or realities.

H2	Portals
HR
P	There are places throughout the world that touch each other on a fundamental level, despite being hundreds of miles apart.
P	The Makers knew how to create portals in such places, allowing for instantaneous travel between them. One might find such a portal…
E	beneath the <b>Ruined Tower</b> (page 332)
E	in the <b>Labyrinth</b> (page 242)
E	hidden away near <b>Three Coven Lake</b> (page 438)
E	among the ruins of <b>Vor Svetelik</b> (page 468)
E	up on <b>Tor's Fist</b> (page 481), perhaps
E	maybe in certain ruins down in <b>Lygos</b> <b>and the South</b> (page 256)
E	anywhere else you think makes sense.
P	Portals can be activated via <b>Opening the</b> <b>Way</b> (page 517), which requires inscribing the sigil sequence of one portal within the sigils of another.
P	Should the PCs learn to use portals, they might wish to create new ones. To do so, they must:
C	Locate a suitable site of primordial power
C	Transport a slab of pure white stone (Value 2 or 3, depending on size) to the site
C	Discern the correct sigil sequence for this site
C	Have an <i>exceptional</i> stonecutter spend a season (Value 2) carving the sigils into the stone
C	Risk damage to the stone or a flawed portal The Makers' portals were safe and stable, but flawed or damaged portals are terribly dangerous. One might explode, tear travelers apart, and/or open a <b>rift</b> (page 311) in the world. See the <b>cracked portal</b> (page 473) of Vor Svetelik for an example.

H2	Black iron
HR
P	A few rare veins of this metal exist in the world, but mostly it's retrieved from meteorites. It is completely, utterly immune to magic.
B	<b>Fae</b> (page 94) treat it like iron, but worse—its touch unravels their magic and they take +1d6 damage (<i>messy</i>, ignores armor) from it
B	Spirits can't touch it, perhaps can't even perceive it
B	It can damage even insubstantial forms of manifest <b>spirits</b> (page 358), but does no true harm to the spirit itself
B	It damages or destroys any open portal it touches, going nowhere
B	Spells, rituals, and other magic cannot affect it, pierce it, detect it, or perceive things enclosed by it
P	When the PCs encounter some, pick or roll for its form:
P	<b>1d12</b> form
HR
P	1-2 Ore/lump/meteorite
P	3-4 Raw material (spool/ingot/rod/etc.)
P	5-6 Charm/talisman/jewelry/symbol
P	7-8 Tool (nail/hammer/tongs/etc.)
P	9-10 Weapon/shield/armor
P	11-12 Construction (door/plating/throne/ etc.), likely <i>immobile</i>
P	Pick or roll for its size and its Value to those who understand what it is. For worked items made of black iron, add their base Value to what's listed below. For example, a sword (Value 1) made of black ◇ iron would be Value 3.
P	<b>1d12</b> size
HR
P	1-4 A small object/amount (Value 1)
P	5-8 A object/amount (Value 2)◇
P	9-11 A ◇◇ object/amount (Value 2)
P	12 An <i>immobile</i> object/amount (Value
P	3 at least)
P	Black iron is strong and hard like steel and worked much the same way. It's a little on the heavy side, and doesn't hold quite as keen an edge. Black iron weapons don't have "<i>x</i> piercing," but a black iron warhammer would still have 2 piercing.

H3	A bejeweled helm
P	◇, <i>magical</i>, <i>loud</i>, <i>dangerous</i>, 1d4+1 uses Bronze, battered, and adorned with seven fittings, 1d4+1 of which bear purple gems that hum ominously. When you <b><i>don the</i></b> <b><i>helm</i></b>, you sense the gems' power and how to use them but can hear nothing over their incessant noise.
P	When you <b><i>unleash a gem's power</i></b>, pick a target you can see and roll +WIS: <b>on a 10+</b>, your target freezes in time and space for as long as you wear the helm and maintain focus; <b>on a 7-9</b>, you must focus for a few seconds, but then the effect kicks in as per a 10+.
P	<b><i>While your target remains frozen</i></b>, the gem hums louder and louder, painfully so. When <b><i>the effect ends</i></b>, the gem crumbles to dust.
P	When you <b><i>try to maintain focus</i></b>, roll
P	+CON: <b>on a 10+</b>, you're fine for now; <b>on a</b> <b>7-9</b>, either mark a debility or let the effect end; <b>on a 6-</b>, mark a debility and either let the effect end or ask the GM how time and space start to go haywire around you.
P	While frozen, the target (and anything on their person) is inviolate—they cannot be harmed, moved, or otherwise interacted with. They rejoin the timeline as if no time had passed for them, with whatever momentum they previously had.

ICON	icons/treasure.svg
H3	A sealed amphora
P	◇◇, <i>fragile</i>, <i>magical</i>, 3 uses
P	A ceramic, two-armed jug with a wax seal.
P	Inside is water of life, the quintessence of water, so pure that it washes away all impurity, corruption, poison, or disease from any living thing. It becomes sullied and loses its potency when used, or if left unsealed for more than a minute or so.
P	The amphora itself is a perfect vessel: as long as it is sealed, no substance within will rot, putrefy, or otherwise spoil.
ICON	icons/treasure.svg
H3	A fossilized horn
P	◇, <i>magical</i>
P	A spiral thing, maybe 2' long, the remnant of some long-gone <b>incarnation</b> (page 300). Those sensitive to the spirit world can sense its lingering, radiant power.
P	When you <b><i>bear the fossilized horn</i></b>, you have advantage on any move to impress, intimidate, or threaten a spirit (though it grants no special ability to communicate with spirits in the first place). Should you roll a 6- on any such roll, the spirit can choose to destroy the horn and end its effect, in addition to whatever else the GM says.

ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Fate
P	Threat (<i>affliction</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to push towards the inevitable
P	There are those whose fates are heralded by prophecy, omen, and vision. And if you know your fate, maybe, just maybe, you can change it.
P	• Reveal that recent events were foretold long ago
P	• Reveal things yet to come
P	• Use coincidence to push them towards their fate
P	• Show how attempts to avert fate actually brings it to pass
P	• Offer an opportunity to change their fate, but tell them the costs/consequences of doing so
HR
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Incomprehensible knowledge
P	Threat (<i>affliction</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to unravel any sense of safety/self
P	When one delves into primordial mysteries, one must grapple with alien and unsettling ideas. Dwell on them too long, and you find your mind turning against itself.
C	You fidget, fixate, have trouble sleeping or relaxing
C	Change your instinct to… (pick 1)
C	Paranoia: To invent dangers
C	Compulsion: To obsessively repeat certain actions
C	Apathy: To let things escalate
C	Henceforth, when the GM compels you to act on your instinct, mark XP if you do and Defy Danger if you don't
C	<b>Impending doom</b>: Retire your PC; they become a threat (a <i>wildcard</i>)
PAGE	311
HR
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Primordial flame
P	<i>Primordial</i>, <i>terrifying</i>, <i>magical</i>
P	<b>Damage</b> 1d12 w/advantage (<i>hand</i>, <i>messy</i>, ignores armor)
P	• Radiate blistering heat, 1d10 damage (<i>reach</i>, <i>area</i>)
P	• Start normal fires nearby
P	• Reduce what it touches to ash
P	A tongue of perfect blue fire, somehow brought into the world. It is likely found held in stasis by some potent magic or artifice. For while it consumes and destroys all it touches, it cannot last long in contact with base reality.
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Rift
P	When primordial power runs amok, it can damage reality itself. Such rifts might manifest as places where:
B	Time runs slowly/quickly/not at all
B	Things emerge from other times/ places/realities
B	Natural laws like light, heat, gravity, and death behave strangely
B	The world breaks down into chemics/ crystals/raw elements
B	New lifeforms/consciousnesses arise
B	<b>Fundamentals</b> (page 312), <b>voidblights</b> (page 313), or other dangerous spirits enter the world
B	The Things Below spread their influence (see <b>corrupted sites</b>, page 422)
P	Most rifts are temporary, soon sealed by <b>archons</b> (page 302) or other primordial entities. But if one persists for any length of time, write it up as a threat (a <i>MacGuffin</i>, <b>Instinct</b> to unravel reality).
PAGE	312

H3	Fundamental
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>primordial</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 19; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks vitals), harmed only by black iron <b>Damage</b> destructive touch 1d10 w/advantage (<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>, ignores armor)
P	<b>Instinct</b> see below
P	• Manifest in the proper conditions
P	• Communicate poorly
P	• Burden with <b>incomprehensible</b> <b>knowledge</b> (page 310)
P	• Refuse to cooperate
P	• Manipulate/manifest its element, locally and dramatically
P	These are <b>spirits</b> (page 358) of fundamental forces, far removed from mortal concerns. They are active only near sites of primordial power and uncontrolled <b>rifts</b> (page 311), or when called forth by powerful, dangerous magic.
P	Example fundamentals include:

ICON	icons/spirit.svg
H3	Voidblight
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>primordial</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>hungry</i>, <i>cautious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 10; <b>Armor</b> 1 (lacks vitals)
P	<b>Damage</b> spirit-rending bite d6+2 (<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> can harm only spirits and mortals sensitive to the spirit world; harmed only by other spirits or magic attacks
P	<b>Instinct</b> to eat and spawn
P	• Follow the "scent" of a rift or a spirit-walker
P	• Mimic a spirit it has eaten
P	• Pounce on unsuspecting prey
P	• After a good meal: spawn another of its kind
P	To those who can perceive them, they seem like many-limbed salamanders made of starfilled night. Their broad, flat, eyeless heads split open into rows of glittering teeth.
P	They are alien things, spiritual scavengers and predators. They haunt forgotten corners of the spirit world, the dead worldmotes that float through the cosmic void.
P	Mostly, they wait and hunger. But if they catch the scent of a traveler, or worse, a <b>rift</b> (page 311) into our world, they will follow it.
P	Treat an incursion of voidblights as a threat (type: <i>beasts</i>) with the following grim portents:
C	A few local spirits are killed; others are spooked; sensitive mortals are unnerved
C	"Softer" local spirits die or flee; plants fail, animals grow sickly, misfortune abounds; voidblights attack sensitive mortals
C	Almost all local spirits flee or are eaten; local systems collapse and die
C	<b>Impending doom</b>: voidblights spread into new colonies, all over the region and soon the world <b>Stakes</b>: Will any of the PCs' enemies join them to face this threat? How will the environment be permanently changed? What will happen if the voidblights are corrupted by the Things Below?
HR
H3	Other primordial entities
B	The <b>Things Below</b> (page 412)
B	<b>Great spirits</b> (page 300), possibly including the <b>Lady of Crows</b> (page 71) and some or all of the major <b>gods</b> (page 178)
B	<b>Incarnations</b> (page 300), including the <b>Willow Witches</b> (page 120) and perhaps the <b>Nine-fingered stranger</b> (page 457) and/or the <b>Pale Hunter</b> (page 292)
B	<b>Archons</b> (page 302), including <b>Tcaventes, Shackle and Key</b> (page 254)
B	<b>Titans</b> (page 303), perhaps including the <b>Crombil</b> (page 62) and/or the <b>Suileach</b> (page 93)
